To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) cellular access is more consistent than WiFi, but WiFi is more consistent than fixed line access, and (ii) WiFi is better for download throughput but cellular access is better for upload throughput and latency.

(1) WiFi performance is more consistent, (2) cellular performance varies widely with location and time, (3) WiFi performance varies widely with service provider and location, and (4) cellular and WiFi are complementary technologies.

(i) cellular performance varies significantly with time of day and across metro areas; (ii) cellular performance varies with cell technology; (iii) WiFi performance varies across metro areas, and with WiFi access type; (iv) cellular performance is more consistent than WiFi performance; and (v) cellular performance varies across providers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether cell or WiFi provides better performance for mobile users.
understanding the performance characteristics of cellular and WiFi networks in diverse metro areas.
the performance of mobile Internet connectivity in the real world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single answer to the question of which is best.
the performance of cellular and WiFi is very dependent on the specific access technology, the service provider, and the location.
cellular and WiFi performance varies significantly with time, space, and access type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WiFi and cellular are complementary technologies that provide a range of performance options for mobile users, and that the best option for a user will vary based on their use context.

WiFi and cell access provide very different performance characteristics, with WiFi generally offering better performance but at the cost of coverage, and that performance is highly dependent on the local environment.
cellular and WiFi performance is highly variable and that the performance differences are significant enough to warrant consideration when selecting a technology for use in a particular application.

there are significant differences in performance and consistency between cellular and WiFi, and that performance varies widely across different areas, access technologies, and service providers.
